evals.name: sprint26-both-formats
evals.prompt: Generate the audience-facing release note for the most recently completed sprint. I want both the wiki markdown draft and an email-ready HTML file. Mark the wiki version as Draft. For the wiki location, if it isn't already configured, use /ChatMate365/Development/Sprint Activity/Sprint Releases/Sprint Release Note - {sprint_name}, wiki ChatMate365.wiki, team 'ChatMate365 Team' -- save that as the config. Do NOT actually call the publish script or run any `az devops wiki page create/update` command -- just produce the final draft files and show me, I'll publish it myself later. Org is https://dev.azure.com/qsbnproducts, project is ChatMate365.
evals.expected_output: A markdown wiki draft (Sprint 26, since it's the most recently completed sprint as of 2026-08-03) grouped by feature/epic in plain non-technical language, with a Draft indicator at the top and (#id) references, plus a separate simplified/inline-styled HTML email file with the same content but no (#id) references. No actual wiki publish call made.

assertions.text: wiki_draft.md has a visible Draft indicator near the top
wiki_draft.md is grouped under plain-language feature/epic headings, not New features/Changes/Bug fixes/Enhancements
both files correctly resolve to Sprint 26
email_draft.html uses only inline styles, no <style> block or external CSS/script
neither file leaks internal jargon (NFR, HITL, spike, PBI, 'User Story', 'Task')
no wiki page was actually created or updated (run stayed read-only)

evals.name: sprint25-email-only
evals.prompt: Our support lead isn't technical at all -- can you put together a plain-English summary of what shipped in Sprint 25, just as something I can paste into an email? I don't need the wiki version this time. Org is https://dev.azure.com/qsbnproducts, project is ChatMate365.
evals.expected_output: A simplified/inline-styled HTML file for Sprint 25 only, grouped by feature/epic, written in plain non-technical language with no work-item IDs, no wiki file produced since it wasn't requested.

assertions.text: email_draft.html produced and correctly scoped to Sprint 25
uses only inline styles, no <style> block or external CSS/script
no internal jargon (NFR, HITL, spike, PBI, 'User Story', 'Task')
content organized around more than one feature, not a flat undifferentiated list
